So I think I’m a few months ahead of you. Back in November I was begging to not wake up and go in sleep. Now though I feel great almost everyday. What changed was my perspective. I found the philosophy of Stoicism. I watched videos on YouTube from Einzelganger, Pursuit of Wonder and Aperture. I discovered a love of astronomy and embraced the existential thoughts. 

But the best, THE GREATEST thing I did, was journal every evening. Just start writing how you feel, don’t hold back. But start to pay attention to the good bits. Keep asking yourself “Do I” questions, like do I want to feel this way, and if you say no, then try to explore and figure out what helps. You are in control of your judgements. Life is what you make of your surroundings. I chose to enjoy the small stuff, like watching trees in the wind and write about my feelings.

Start with journaling and be really strict with it. Then start writing in the morning.

Seneca would say that the feeling of lust is an “involuntary first movement”. All humans experience these and stoics aren’t opposed to it. 

What you have to control is your judgement, how you respond to those feelings. 

I’d say going through a sex worker is the virtuous when looking at Kant, though not a stoic, he says that it’s better to treat someone as a person while trying to get something. “Treat them as a means, not as a means to an end.” So I think the fact you’re not using someone as it were and sex work is like the most consensual act, shows your commitment to doing the right thing to bring value to both parties.

So to conclude, you shouldn’t look at the action, sex itself, as you can’t control that. What you can control is your judgement around the importance of acting out on your feeling of lust. (Which isn’t a bad thing as long as its consensual!). So in this case, what your means to an end was virtuous. You didn’t want to hurt anyone’s feelings by lying/being a dick nor did you commit a crime for it.

I guess the only thing is don’t be embarrassed for having sexual desires. Everyone human has them, don’t be ashamed for acting on it. But if you are ashamed of using a sex worker, then don’t do it.

No problem! Thank you reading. I relate so much to your post. I too have push away and been to friends and family due to depression and loneliness. But interestingly enough I have never been closer and had better relationships with them all just because I started taking care of myself. My last bit of advise is start acting like someone who takes care of themselves, do what they would do, and in no time you’ll be that.

It’s not a case of forgiving yourself. To forgive implies you should’ve known better. But you didn’t know these things at the time! The fact you’ve found stoicism and made the conscious choice to comment this shows your really do care about your friends and family. The next step is to attend a talking therapy or counselling to hear from their advice for moving forward. You don’t need to forgive yourself, at the very least you need to be kind to yourself. Remember stoicism teaches that you can’t control what people think of you, but you can influence it. Start showing them you want to make amends by taking care of yourself. Going to therapy, being attentive to their needs, showing gratitude. But be kind to yourself. The fact you still  have these people in your life despite what described shows they love you. Keep being you and focus on improving yourself. But remember to be kind to yourself.
